review.note: Attributed to a Reformed author. Not reviewed against the Westminster Confession. Gap-fill source, two scopes. (1) 2026-09-24 (workstream M, 0.9.5): the app's primary 'calvin' source (Pillar/CrossWire conversion) has empty content for Isaiah 49-66 -- the entire Book of Consolation, including the Servant Songs and Isaiah 53 -- confirmed as a genuine upstream gap (a fresh fetch of the same Pillar conversion is also empty for these chapters), not a local corruption. HelloAO's independent digitization of the same underlying commentary has real content for all 18 of these chapters, verified against the Pillar copy's Isaiah 1 to be the same translation. (2) 2026-09-24 (workstream R2, 0.10): the Psalms. The Pillar conversion repeats one block per psalm under every verse for 148 of 150 chapters; HelloAO has the real per-verse commentary (e.g. Ps 22:16 on 'they have pierced'), verified against the Pillar text the two share (>= 90% of every chapter's shared 6-word shingles; see data/study-build-report.json 'calvinPsalms'). Emitted only for ISA 49-66 and the PSA chapters where Pillar has only the repeated block; in a given psalm this source's per-verse text never sits beside a Pillar per-verse entry, and the only Pillar text kept beside it is the psalm's introduction (absent from this digitization). The translator's editorial footnotes (partly in French) and their inline [n] markers are not shipped. See work-content/helloao/calvin-helloao/_fetch-manifest.json and CONTENT-SOURCES.md.

matthew-henry.publisher: Digitized by the HelloAO Free Use Bible API from the historic public-domain Commentary on the Whole Bible

review.note: Attributed to a Reformed author. Not reviewed against the Westminster Confession. Henry completed Genesis through Acts himself; Romans onward was finished after his 1714 death by other nonconformist ministers from his notes -- long-published and treated as one continuous work, as it is here. Verified 2026-09-22, directly against this digitization's own books.json and chapter files, not assumed: it covers 65 of 66 books (no Song of Solomon at all) and three of those 65 are themselves truncated -- 2 Samuel stops at chapter 22 of 24, Jonah at chapter 1 of 4, and Matthew at chapter 18 of 28 (missing 19-28: the Olivet Discourse, Last Supper, Gethsemane, crucifixion and resurrection accounts). A further 8 chapters are individually empty within otherwise-complete books (Numbers 31-35, Joshua 22-23, Psalm 72) -- confirmed genuinely empty in the source ('content': []), not a parsing failure. None of this leaves any chapter of the Bible with zero Reformed commentary overall -- Calvin and/or Gill still cover every gap -- but Henry's own voice is absent there. See data/study-build-report.json.
